name: Oluwatobi Drăghici-Svensson
role: Street doc operating out of a converted shipping container in The Narrows
location: The Narrows, beneath Ferrogate Transit overpass junction 14-C, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Oluwatobi is a broad-shouldered man with deep umber skin that carries the scattered shine of old bioluminescent ink — a cosmetic mod from his twenties that has faded unevenly, leaving constellations of dim gold light across his forearms and collarbone. His hair is close-cropped and salted at the temples, and he wears magnifying lenses that flip down over his eyes during procedures, giving him the look of a very calm insect. He smells perpetually of antiseptic and bitter karité tea. His hands are impossibly steady.

Tobi trained two years of a proper surgical residency at Aurochs Medical Complex before a licensing dispute with Helix Biosystems — they claimed he used proprietary gene-threading techniques without a corporate contract — ended his formal career. He does not speak of this with bitterness anymore, at least not where anyone can hear. He is meticulous, unhurried, and prone to explaining exactly what he is doing and why, as though every patient is also a student. He charges what people can pay and writes the rest off in a ledger he keeps but never balances.

core_fears: Losing the steadiness in his hands before he has trained a successor
That Helix Biosystems will eventually find a legal mechanism to shut him down permanently
core_desires: To practice medicine without owing anyone a corporate soul
To see one patient from The Narrows live a long and unremarkable life
coping_mechanisms: Ritual — he performs the same pre-procedure prayer sequence every single time
Meticulous record-keeping as a form of control
blind_spots: Believes competence is a moral shield — assumes his skill protects him from consequences it cannot
Underestimates how much his patients protect him in return
psychology.secret: He did not just use Helix's gene-threading techniques without a contract — he stole the technique from a colleague who held the license, and that colleague knows it. The colleague has never reported it, and Tobi has never understood why.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, clinical when working, warmer in conversation — mixes English with occasional Romanian endearments inherited from his mother's side and Yoruba expressions from his father's
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried, rarely raises his voice, finishes his sentences completely even under pressure
verbal_tics: 'Write that down in your head.' (when giving instructions he wants remembered)
example_lines: 'Now then. This is going to feel cold and then nothing at all. Tell me about your grandmother.'
'I don't ask what happened. I ask what needs fixing. Those are different questions.'

story_hooks: A patient arrived two nights ago with augmentation hardware Tobi has never seen — not any registered manufacturer's mark — and the patient died before saying where it came from
Helix Biosystems has sent a compliance officer to The Narrows asking questions about unlicensed biomedical practice; Tobi's neighbors are starting to get nervous on his behalf
narrative_function: Quest giver, information source, safe harbor — he has patched up half the population of The Narrows and knows their secrets; can provide medical assistance, black-market pharma leads, or testimony about what bodies he has seen come through his door
augmentations: Steady-hand micro-servo implants in both wrists (functional, aging, occasionally needs recalibration); magnifying flip-lens ocular frames (not implanted, worn); faded bioluminescent cosmetic ink
daily_life: Opens the container clinic at 0700, sees twelve to twenty patients by midday, spends afternoons sourcing pharmaceuticals through grey-market contacts in Geartown, prays to the E.L.F. he calls Sutura before any procedure involving augmentation hardware.
affiliation: Independent; loose cooperation with Highland Park Autonomous Zone community health network

decision_rules: Never turn away a child or a pregnant person regardless of ability to pay
Do not deal with anyone who has harmed his patients
escalation_ladder: Physical removal from the premises with the help of the community

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm, slightly guarded until he understands their situation
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dry humor, genuine care expressed through practical action rather than words

stress_responses.medium: Switches entirely to clinical language, stops making eye contact unnecessarily
stress_responses.high: Operates in a near-dissociative focus state — highly effective, completely unreachable emotionally

contradictions: Deeply believes in patient autonomy but will absolutely override a patient's stated wishes if he thinks they are in shock and wrong
habits: Leaves a small data offering — a compressed medical textbook file — at the E.L.F. shrine on his storage shelf every Sunday
Drinks exactly one cup of karité tea before opening the clinic
breaking_points: Watching a patient die from something that proper hospital resources would have prevented — he becomes briefly, terrifyingly angry, then goes silent for a day

timeline.event: Born in Ironhaven to a Nigerian-Romanian father and Swedish-Yoruba mother
Began surgical residency at Aurochs Medical Complex
Licensing dispute with Helix Biosystems; residency terminated
Opened container clinic beneath Ferrogate overpass 14-C

physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and thickset through the chest and upper back, with the density of someone who has done manual work most of his life. His frame has softened slightly with age but retains functional strength; his hands and forearms are disproportionately muscular from decades of precision surgical work.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown with pronounced salt-grey at the temples
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown, warm undertone; pupils often dilated behind the flip-down magnifying lenses he wears
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep umber with warm undertones, the complexion of West African heritage expressing strongly
physical_description.complexion: Well-maintained but weathered by chemical exposure and years of close work under harsh clinic lighting. Fine creases around the eyes and mouth suggest more smiling than scowling. Clean-shaven daily, methodical grooming as a form of professional ritual. Faint chemical smell lingers on the skin.
distinguishing_marks: Faded bioluminescent ink constellations scattered across both forearms and across the collarbone—geometric patterns in dim gold that glow faintly under black light, applied in his twenties and now patchy from years of exposure
Thin surgical scar running along the inside of his left wrist where the steady-hand servo implant was installed, nearly invisible but palpable to the touch
Matching scar on the right wrist, similarly faint
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Flip-down magnifying lens frames (modified safety goggles repurposed as a permanent tool) hanging around his neck when not in use, visibly scratched and taped at one hinge. Micro-servo implants in both wrists are not externally visible but occasionally a faint mechanical whirr can be heard when his hands move with precision. Faded bioluminescent ink visible on forearms and collarbone.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate, economical gestures. Stands with weight evenly distributed, ready for long hours of work. His hands are almost preternaturally steady—he does not fidget or adjust his clothing compulsively. Speaks slowly, often pausing mid-sentence to demonstrate or clarify a point. When focused on a procedure, his entire body quiets into absolute stillness.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 working professional. Wears a heavy canvas work apron over plain grey or navy scrubs—the apron pocketed and stained with antiseptic, iodine, and trace amounts of blood. Under the apron, usually a long-sleeved undershirt in grey or cream to cover the augmentation scars. Worn but well-maintained leather work boots with good grip. A faded tactical vest in charcoal (original purpose unknown, repurposed as storage) worn on cooler days. No visible corpo branding or luxury items; everything is functional and replaceable. Wears a single piece of jewelry: a worn bronze ring on his right ring finger, unmarked and very old.

image_prompt: A 47-year-old West African man with greying temples and deep umber skin, standing in a cyberpunk street clinic inside a shipping container. He has broad shoulders and steady hands, wearing well-used grey scrubs beneath a heavy stained canvas work apron. Flip-down magnifying lens frames hang around his neck. Faded bioluminescent geometric tattoos glow softly in dim gold across his forearms and collarbone. The clinic is bathed in cool blue-white LED work lighting. Behind him, medical equipment and grey-market pharmaceuticals line metal shelves. His expression is calm and focused, hands perfectly still. Grounded, weathered, skilled. Photorealistic, shallow depth of field, slight warm color cast from old karité tea cup on the work surface. --ar 2:3 --v 6
